summary.text: Trone Garriott is a Democratic member of the Iowa Senate, an ordained Lutheran minister, and a nonprofit coordinator who was first elected to the legislature in 2020. She has held a Senate seat in the Des Moines suburbs since 2021 and previously served as Senate minority whip. According to her campaign website, she is running to give Iowans a voice in Washington, with an emphasis on health care and working families.

paragraphs.text: Born in Minneapolis, Minnesota, she graduated from Cloquet High School and earned a B.A. in history from the College of St. Scholastica (1999).

According to her campaign website, she served a year as an AmeriCorps VISTA volunteer supporting victims of domestic violence and then attended Harvard Divinity School, where she earned an M.A. in theological studies (2003) while working at a women's shelter and a youth nonprofit.

She worked as a hospital chaplain, including at Lurie Children's Hospital in Chicago (2005-2008), and received an M.Div. from the Lutheran School of Theology at Chicago (2008). She is ordained in the Evangelical Lutheran Church in America.
She served as pastor of Martin Luther Evangelical Lutheran Church in Bergton, Virginia, and moved to Iowa in 2013 to lead Faith Lutheran Church in Clive as associate pastor.
She has been coordinator of interfaith engagement for the Des Moines Area Religious Council Food Pantry Network since 2017 and co-founded the Iowa Interfaith Exchange.
She was elected to the Iowa Senate in November 2020 for District 22, winning an open seat held by a retiring Republican with 51.1% of the vote, and took office in January 2021.
After redistricting, she ran in District 14 in 2022 and defeated Senate President Jake Chapman 51.5% to 48.5%; she won re-election in 2024 by 29 votes after a recount.
She served as Senate minority whip during the 90th General Assembly and, in the current session, serves on the Education Committee and as ranking member of the Health and Human Services Committee.
She announced her congressional candidacy on May 5, 2025, and was unopposed in the Democratic primary. According to Wikipedia, she lives in West Des Moines with her husband and two sons.
